purpose: An editorial selection for this exhibition, not an objective ranking of art history. Narrative order follows the voyage and its Trojan-war background, not the order of Homer's narration or verified real-world geography.
selectionCriteria: Odyssey recognition and direct narrative relevance
Useful source resolution at the intended display size
Different locations and the full Troy-to-Ithaca arc

entries.role: Participation: the expression is the invitation.
entries.why: Odysseus's upturned face gives the participation section an immediate, human emotional hook. The full painting remains available in the artwork viewer.

entries.role: Project statement: a voyage larger than one card.
entries.why: Turner's vast illuminated sea and ship communicate scale, atmosphere and the cost of pride. Keep the horizon and ship rather than reducing this to an anonymous gradient.

entries.role: Temptation story panel beside the Studio-rendered Circe.
entries.why: The cup, frontal figure and reflected world make Circe instantly recognisable. Display the upright composition intact; the card provides a separate game interpretation.

entries.role: Monsters story panel beside Scylla.
entries.why: The immense waves and pale cliff-side figures make the strait a place, not just a monster portrait.

entries.role: Painting material panel.
entries.why: The separation of the standing traveller and seated Calypso creates an exceptionally clear emotional landscape. Let its silence contrast with the violent sea scenes.

entries.book: Trojan-war background; recalled in Odyssey VIII
entries.role: Printmaking panel and the beginning of the route.
entries.why: The horse and surrounding city make Troy unmistakable. Preserve the print as an object, then allow full-resolution inspection.

entries.book: A later visual retelling of multiple episodes
entries.role: Existing opening splash and its associated Long Way Home candidate.
entries.why: Keep the successful panoramic opening. The same work's appearance within its own card is an intentional artwork-to-card relationship, not recycled wallpaper.

entries.role: Blink and return mechanic panel.
entries.why: Athena revealing the island gives return a literal landscape. Keep the coast visible and put text outside the faces.

entries.book: Iliadic background, not an Odyssey episode
entries.role: Stone material panel.
entries.why: Hector and Andromache establish the human cost of the Trojan world. Do not relabel these figures as Odysseus and Penelope.

entries.role: Clay material panel.
entries.why: The ship, mast-bound hero and bird-bodied Sirens communicate an unmistakably ancient Odyssey. Retain the photograph credit as well as the painter attribution.

entries.book: Later mythological reception; not a depicted voyage episode
entries.role: Metal material panel.
entries.why: The bronze object introduces another material and scale. The alabaster base does not make the main figure a stone sculpture.

entries.emotion: The war follows the sailors home
entries.role: Paper material panel.
entries.why: Primaticcio's red-chalk study supplies the often-missed first landfall after Troy and a distinctive warm drawing surface.

entries.role: First tile in Along the way.
entries.why: A direct episode image gives the Lotus-Eaters a setting rather than substituting unrelated botanical lotus imagery.

entries.role: Second tile in Along the way.
entries.why: The crowded harbour and attack broaden the geography beyond the best-known monsters. Use the full scene rather than repeating a giant's isolated head.

entries.emotion: A gift that could change everything
entries.role: Manifest Fate mechanic panel.
entries.why: The exchange of the winds is a legible turning point. This is an editorial pairing with the mechanic, not a claim that the painting depicts its rules.

entries.role: Gods, enchantments and Theros callbacks panel.
entries.why: Fuseli's supernatural figures supply an emotional and tonal break from Mediterranean sunlight. Retain the catalogue attribution rather than inventing new character labels.

entries.chapter: Thrinacia: the cattle of the Sun
entries.role: Survival and Ordeals mechanic panel.
entries.why: A direct Helios-cattle scene connects survival with a consequential choice and adds an essential late-voyage stop.

entries.role: Third tile in Along the way.
entries.why: The meeting in a broad outdoor setting gives the visitor a recognisable landfall and an emotional release after storms and captivity.

entries.role: Homecoming story panel.
entries.why: The quiet encounter completes the human story without another spectacular battle. Do not force a more exact episode identification than the recorded title supports.

entries.role: Final tile in Along the way.
entries.why: Father and son in the vineyard carry the route beyond the suitors and the marital reunion. The exhibition should reach the epic's final book.
